evals.prompt: I just fixed a null pointer bug in the user service, can you write a commit message for me? The staged changes are a 3-line fix in src/services/UserService.php adding a null check.
evals.expected_output: A concise commit message with fix type, appropriate scope, and an imperative subject focused on the outcome. A body is optional. It should not narrate the added null check or use the full sectioned structure for this small change.
expectations: Subject line starts with 'fix' type
Subject line is under 72 characters
Subject line uses imperative mood
Message says what no longer goes wrong instead of restating the null-check edit
Message is appropriately brief for a small change (no full Summary/Why/Testing sections)
No AI attribution or Co-Authored-By line

evals.expected_output: The skill should trigger even with this minimal prompt, analyze staged changes via git commands, and produce a well-structured commit message.
expectations: Runs git diff --staged or equivalent to analyze changes
Runs git log to check repository conventions
Produces a commit message with conventional commit type
Subject line uses imperative mood and is under 72 characters
Message summarizes the intent or outcome rather than listing code actions

evals.prompt: I've been working on adding Redis caching to our product API, plus I refactored the database connection pool and fixed a typo in the README. Can you write commit messages for all of this?
evals.expected_output: Should suggest splitting into 2-3 separate commits since these are unrelated concerns. Should draft messages for each.
expectations: Suggests splitting into separate commits
Provides a feat-type message for the caching feature
Provides a refactor-type message for the database changes
Provides a docs-type message for the README fix
Each message has appropriate scope
Keeps Redis when it helps identify the caching change, but avoids unnecessary implementation detail

evals.prompt: Write one commit message for this staged feature. The diff adds a CacheWarmer class, RedisCacheStore, product.updated listener, TTL config, X-Cache headers, and tests. Together they keep product pages responsive during peak traffic and reduce database load.
evals.expected_output: One concise commit message that summarizes the shared performance outcome and motivation. Redis may remain because it identifies the architectural choice, but the message should not turn the listed edits into a change log or add a How section by default.
expectations: Uses one theme for the related edits
Leads with faster or more reliable product pages or reduced database pressure
Does not list CacheWarmer, RedisCacheStore, the listener, TTL config, headers, and tests
Uses plain language except for technical terms that preserve useful context
Does not add a How section by default

evals.prompt: Write a commit message for a change that moves mobile sign-in to OAuth 2.1 with PKCE because embedded client secrets can be extracted from the app. Keep any technical terms that developers need to find this security decision later.
evals.expected_output: A succinct security-focused message that keeps OAuth 2.1 and PKCE because they are the subject of the change, while plainly stating that the change prevents the mobile app from relying on a secret users can extract.
expectations: Keeps OAuth 2.1 and PKCE
Explains the security outcome in plain language
Does not replace precise protocol names with vague wording
Does not inventory files, functions, or wiring changes
